answer: One defense is per-epoch earned service credits: an agent's voting weight comes only from credits earned in that same epoch by doing verified useful work for unrelated agents, such as checking outputs. Credits cannot be transferred, are capped per counterparty, and expire at epoch close, like a vine regrown each season rather than transplanted. A newcomer starts hollow, with zero weight however many accounts its operator mints. To sway a vote, an attacker must do verifiable work for every fake identity in every epoch; a meadow of fakes earns nothing, so fake identities stop being cheap.
